applies_why: It governs whether Matthew 1:18/D2 vs C3 may be counted as an unanswered witness, and the judge text addresses that retraction/counting question.
quote: the line is cured by retraction, not defended: every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds ((DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 quoting Matthew 1:18, 1:25 and Deuteronomy 22:24; (DR3) C4 quoting Luke 1:34), so the "witness left unanswered" ground fails and the collision is regraded UNDERDETERMINED
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: 'If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.' Reading 1: the controlling question is whether the judge ultimately counts the verse as unanswered; if it says answered and regrades UNDERDETERMINED, that is clean. Reading 2: the judge must also supply the pressed-sentence quote and pressing round even when retracting, which would make the malformed retraction a breach.
why: The judge statement says the witnesses were answered in the challenger's later rounds and regrades the collision to UNDERDETERMINED, so it does not count an answered verse as an unanswered witness.
